options.text: A culture and set of practices uniting development and operations through shared ownership, automation, and fast feedback

questions.explanation: DevOps is primarily a culture of shared ownership and fast feedback, supported by automation — not just a tool or product.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?

options.text: Continuous delivery keeps a human approval before the production deploy; continuous deployment deploys every passing change automatically

questions.explanation: Both make passing changes releasable. Delivery keeps a manual gate before production; deployment removes that gate and ships automatically.

questions.prompt: Why is a container image an ideal artifact for a CI/CD pipeline?

options.text: Because it must be rebuilt for each environment
Because it is immutable and versioned, so you build once and promote the exact same image from staging to production
Because it stores configuration inside the image
Because it cannot be pushed to a registry

questions.explanation: An image is an immutable, versioned artifact bundling app and dependencies, so the thing you tested is exactly the thing you deploy.

questions.prompt: The practice of merging small changes frequently with an automated build and test on each is called continuous ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Continuous integration merges changes often and runs automated build and tests to catch integration problems early.

questions.prompt: Which twelve-factor habits help containers thrive in CI/CD? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep configuration in the environment, not baked into the image
Keep processes stateless, storing state in backing services
Write logs to stdout/stderr as event streams
Hard-code production secrets into the image

questions.explanation: Config in the environment, stateless processes, and logs as streams all fit the container model. Baking secrets into the image is the opposite of good practice.

questions.prompt: Order the typical stages of a CI/CD pipeline.

items.text: Package it as a container image and push to a registry

questions.explanation: After a commit triggers the pipeline, it builds, tests, packages/publishes the image, and then deploys and operates it.
